historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-9% / -16%) and unusable as the growth anchor: book equity was cut by the 7.5bn buyback programme and the 2.5bn impairment, not by operations. GAAP EPS CAGR is distorted by the same impairment (FY2025 EPS 1.54 vs adjusted 4.85). Revenue 5-year CAGR is used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, net debtor): FY2020 3,765, FY2022 1,230, FY2025 3,299 (Kroger fiscal years; CSV labels are one year later). SBC is ~0.1% of sales, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively identical. The series is dominated by working-capital swings (3-year +39%, 5-year -3%) and carries little signal; the 3-year revenue CAGR of -0.1% reflects falling fuel prices and the Kroger Specialty Pharmacy sale, while identical sales ex fuel grew 0.9%, 1.5% and 2.9% in the last three fiscal years.

scenario_narratives.base: Kroger holds its regional share but does not win it back. Identical sales ex fuel recover from ~0.5% in fiscal 2026 to 2.0-2.5%, short of the ~3% management targets for FY2029, as pharmacy reimbursement (IRA) and brand-to-generic mix keep dragging. Retail media and data (alternative profit, ~1.5bn of operating profit) grow and the closed Ocado fulfilment centres stop losing money, which pays for the price investment needed against Walmart, Costco and Aldi: adjusted EBITDA margin after LIFO goes from 5.25% back to 5.5%, EBITDA grows ~3% a year, the bottom of the 3-6% target. Capex stays above depreciation as store projects accelerate under the new CEO. Giant Eagle is treated as value-neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: Greg Foran's Walmart playbook works: store standards, fresh and price perception improve, comps reach the 3% target by FY2028 and hold near it, with eCommerce growing mid-teens on the store-fulfilled model. Kroger Precision Marketing and 84.51 scale off the 63m-household loyalty base and carry the mix; with the fulfilment losses gone and corporate cost taken out, margin expands to 5.9% and EBITDA compounds ~5% a year, inside the upper half of the target range. This needs share gains in a market where Kroger is currently losing traffic, plus continued retail-media growth, plus no labour disruption.
scenario_narratives.bear: The fiscal 2026 slowdown is the trend, not a pause: Walmart, Costco, Amazon and the hard discounters keep taking traffic, comps run 0-1% in real-terms decline, and Kroger has to fund price and wage increases (two-thirds of associates are under ~350 union contracts) without the volume to absorb them. Pharmacy economics deteriorate further and agentic or third-party shopping channels weaken the loyalty-data advantage that retail media depends on. Margin slides to 4.9%, capex stays elevated through year six because stores must be defended, and the terminal multiple is capped at 14x for a shrinking-share grocer. The business stays solvent and cash-generative throughout; this is an erosion case, not a distress case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature, defensive, low-growth grocer valued on unlevered owner free cash flow with a 10-year component build. Value is driven by two things: about 25bp of EBITDA margin either way and the gap between capex and depreciation; revenue growth matters little. The terminal cap of 18x (base, bull) sits just below the Gordon value at 7.5% / 2.0%, so the terminal value is close to uncapped in the base case; the bear case is capped at 14x. SBC is only ~0.13% of sales, but on a ~2% free-cash-flow margin that is ~7% of the flow, so the street basis (SBC treated as non-cash) sits ~9% above the house value; the share price falls inside that band. A 15% hurdle is a demanding test for an asset discounted at 7.5%; an entry price near half of intrinsic value is the expected result, not an error. Model approach after the sanity check: the multiples check tripped because the base value implies ~53x trailing earnings, more than twice the 10-year average of 19x. That is the earnings figure, not the valuation: fiscal 2025 GAAP EPS was 1.54 after a 2.5bn write-down of the automated fulfilment network, against 4.85 adjusted, and the shares already trade on ~52x the same depressed figure. On adjusted earnings the base value is ~14x, and on adjusted EBITDA ~7.1x enterprise value against a 10-year average of 7.9x. Each remedy in the fix list was tested and found already in place: projected levered free cash flow starts at ~2.0bn, below the 2.4bn mid-cycle figure and well below the 3.3bn reported for fiscal 2025; the 7.5% discount rate already carries ~1.1 points over the computed 6.4%; growth of 1.8-2.5% is at or below the 5-year revenue CAGR; and the terminal value is ~7.2x EBITDA, under the 10-year average. Forcing a pass would need a base value near 51 a share, about 5.7x adjusted EBITDA and below any multiple Kroger has traded at in ten years, so the values were left unchanged and the trip is recorded as a known false positive. Framing: an income-and-buyback compounder priced close to fair value, not a growth story; the return case rests on margin and capital discipline.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin: each 10bp of EBITDA margin is ~150m of EBITDA, roughly 2.50-3.00 per share of value
Capex intensity: store projects are running ahead of guidance (H1 2.7bn vs 2.0bn); if capex stays near 2.8% of sales rather than falling to 2.45% the base value drops materially
WACC: 7.5% carries an explicit ~1.1 point premium over a computed ~6.4%; at 8.0% the base value falls by roughly a tenth, and the sensitivity grid shows the swing
Giant Eagle is assumed value-neutral; overpayment, forced divestitures or integration cost are not modelled, and the 1.25bn cash outlay will raise net debt when it closes
Albertsons litigation is carried at a 25% probability of the 600m fee only; claimed damages beyond the fee are unquantified
Multi-employer pension underfunding (~1.2bn) is assumed to be funded through operating expense at current contribution rates; a step-up in contributions would come out of margin
Q3 fiscal 2026 results (early December 2026) will be the first read on whether comps have stabilised; year-1 growth and margin should be re-judged then

sanity_check_response.diagnosis: Denominator artifact. FY2026-labelled (Kroger fiscal 2025) GAAP EPS of 1.54 carries the 2.5bn fulfilment-network impairment; adjusted EPS was 4.85. The actual trailing P/E at the fiscal year-end price was already 51.6x. The same impairment depresses reported EBITDA (5,222 vs 8,080 adjusted) and book equity (P/B).

fixes_tested.result: Already satisfied. Mid-point of median (1,447) and latest (3,299) owner FCF = 2,373. Base year-1 levered owner FCF ~2.0bn, years 1-5 average ~2.5bn. Recorded as inputs.mid_cycle_fcf; no driver change.
Already embedded: 7.5% vs computed ~6.4%, now itemised in wacc_rationale. Not raised further.
Already satisfied: base growth 1.8-2.5% then 2.0% vs 5-year revenue CAGR 2.2% and a ~3% management target.
Already satisfied: base terminal value ~7.2x terminal EBITDA vs 10-year average EV/EBITDA 7.9x; bear ~5x vs 10-year minimum 6.0x; bull under the 11.3x maximum.

sanity_check_response.value_needed_to_pass: Base value <= ~50.8 per share (2 x 19.2 x SBC-adjusted EPS ~1.32), i.e. ~5.7x EV/adjusted EBITDA, below the 10-year minimum of 6.0x. Not defensible.
sanity_check_response.what_would_change_this: Q3 fiscal 2026 (early December 2026): if identical sales ex fuel stay near zero and adjusted EBITDA margin falls below the 5.25% year-1 path, re-judge year-1 to year-3 margin and shift weight to the bear case; that, not the P/E rule, is the real downside test. The trip should clear by itself once fiscal 2026 EPS (guided 5.10-5.30 adjusted) replaces the impaired year.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close); 52-week range 54.15-76.58
data_sources.financials: KR_Metrics.csv / KR.duckdb (SEC XBRL); Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (KR_Annual_FY2026.txt); Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 15 Aug 2026 (KR_Quarterly_Q2-2027.txt) for the balance sheet, share count, H1 cash flow, opioid liability and capex commentary
data_sources.qualitative: KR_Analysis.json (2026-11-15), including fiscal 2026 guidance (adjusted EPS 5.10-5.30) and the 20 Oct 2026 Investor Update targets

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at the balance-sheet date: 596m outstanding at 15 Aug 2026 (1,918m issued less 1,322m treasury, Q2 10-Q equity statement) plus 2m dilutive options (Q2 EPS note). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. The 10-Q cover shows 590.6m at 15 Sep 2026; the ~5m shares bought after the balance-sheet date are deliberately not used, because the cash that bought them is still in the 15 Aug cash balance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (year ended 31 Jan 2026) cash flow statement, share-based employee compensation add-back. Kroger publishes no combined equity-award figure and no separate tax-withholding line; withholding is netted inside treasury stock purchases and is not separable, so the add-back is used as is. H1 FY2026 SBC ran 101 vs 83, so the forward path is set at 0.13% of sales, above the 0.106% FY actual.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: Saturday nearest 31 January (FY2026 label = Kroger fiscal 2025, ended 31 Jan 2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.6 (defensive grocer; observed beta is lower) gives cost of equity ~7.3%; pre-tax debt cost ~5% (3.9% after tax). At market weights (~72% equity / 28% debt) the computed WACC is ~6.4%. 7.5% is used: an explicit structural premium of ~1.1 points over the computed rate, which puts the WACC above the CAPM cost of equity itself. The premium is for (a) the leverage step-up (debt 10.2bn to 15.9bn and book equity 11.6bn to 5.9bn in two years on the 7.5bn buyback, with ~1.25bn more cash going out for Giant Eagle), (b) labour and pension structure (two-thirds of associates under ~350 union contracts, ~1.2bn multi-employer pension underfunding off balance sheet) and (c) regulatory exposure in pharmacy reimbursement and SNAP-funded sales. Reviewed after the 2026-11-15 sanity-check trip (candidate: wacc_too_low) and deliberately NOT raised further: no single regulator, customer or licence can stop the business, so the 'regulatory single point of failure' premium does not apply, and a further +0.5 point would cut the base value by roughly a tenth without clearing a trip that comes from impairment-depressed GAAP EPS. One WACC for all three scenarios: risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Under US GAAP (ASC 842) operating-lease rent (872 in FY2025) is an operating expense already inside EBITDA, so the 7,161 of operating lease liabilities at 15 Aug 2026 are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases are inside reported debt (total_debt 16,997 = 1,838 current + 15,159 long-term, including finance lease obligations) and their amortisation sits in D&A. lease_cost_pct_path is omitted because the rent is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial (NCI equity 6 at 15 Aug 2026); no adjustment.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon; fresh build (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Kroger is a single-segment US operating grocer, so the default row of the routing table applies. EBITDA margin is ADJUSTED FIFO EBITDA LESS THE LIFO CHARGE (adjusted FIFO operating profit 4,905 + D&A 3,332 - LIFO 157 = 8,080, 5.47% of FY2025 sales). The reported EBITDA of 5,222 carries the 2.5bn fulfilment-network impairment and is not a base. Calibration: FY0 component build gives unlevered owner FCF of ~3.0bn; less ~0.5bn after-tax interest that is ~2.5bn levered, against reported FCF of 1,420 / 2,884 / 1,777 / 3,456 over the last four fiscal years (average 2.4bn, which includes merger and opioid cash costs). last_fcf (3,299 = 3,456 reported - 157 SBC) is a LEVERED figure after interest paid and flattered by working capital in FY2025; the projections do not compound from it. Interest income is not stripped: Kroger is a net debtor (net debt 15.3bn), so there is no cash pile to double-count. Buybacks are funded (3.4bn in FY2025, 1.3bn in H1 FY2026), so the flat share count is a paid-for convention. Giant Eagle (1.65bn, expected to close in fiscal 2027) is EXCLUDED from flows, revenue and net debt, i.e. treated as value-neutral at the price paid; management's long-term targets also exclude it. Multi-employer pension underfunding (~1.2bn, off balance sheet) is not deducted in the bridge because the contributions run through operating expense and are already in the margin; deducting the stock as well would charge it twice. Working capital capture is zero: a grocer runs payables roughly against inventory, and no growth-driven release is assumed. Q3 FY2026 results are due early December 2026 and are not in this build. SANITY-CHECK FIX PASS (2026-11-15): the multiples check tripped on implied P/E > 2x the 10-year average. Diagnosed as a denominator artifact (GAAP EPS 1.54 after the 2.5bn impairment against adjusted 4.85), not a model error; driver paths, WACC, weights and values are unchanged. See valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response and inputs.mid_cycle_fcf.

mid_cycle_fcf.basis: Mid-point of the historical median owner FCF flagged by the sanity check (1,447) and the latest owner FCF (3,299 = 3,456 reported - 157 SBC). SBC-adjusted throughout.
mid_cycle_fcf.how_used: A ceiling test on the projected flows, not a compounding base: the component route builds FCF from revenue, margin, capex and tax, and never compounds from last_fcf. Base year-1 unlevered owner FCF is ~2.55bn, ~2.0bn after ~0.5bn of after-tax interest, i.e. BELOW the 2,373 mid-cycle figure; the levered average over years 1-5 is ~2.5bn, which is the mid-cycle figure grown at ~2.3% a year for three years. The FY2025 working-capital windfall (operating cash flow 7.3bn against 4.5-6.8bn in the prior three years) is therefore not capitalised anywhere in the model.
mid_cycle_fcf.last_fcf_note: last_fcf stays at 3,299 because it is the audited owner-FCF actual (reported less SBC); it is a peak-ish levered figure and must not be read as the run-rate. Use mid_cycle_fcf for that.

bear.capex_rationale: Capex stays elevated for six years because stores must be defended, then settles at 2.5% against D&A of 2.25%: the same ~1.11x capex-to-depreciation ratio as the base terminal year, so the terminal year is not capitalising a gap that depreciation would close.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 is fiscal 2026 (ending Jan 2027): H1 total sales +2.1%, of which fuel did most of the work; identical sales ex fuel only +0.6% YTD and +0.2% in Q2. Later years reach 2.5%, a haircut to management's ~3% comparable-sales target for FY2029.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 at 5.25% vs 5.47% in FY0: H1 adjusted FIFO operating profit was flat (2,620 vs 2,609) only because D&A fell 103 after the impairment, so H1 EBITDA after LIFO was ~5.27% of sales against ~5.48% a year earlier. Recovery to 5.5% gives EBITDA growth of ~3% a year, the bottom of the 3-6% target range.
base.capex_rationale: Year 1 at 2.8% (~4.2bn): guidance is 'relatively consistent with 2025' (~3.9bn) but H1 capital investments ran 2.7bn vs 2.0bn. Terminal capex 2.45% stays above D&A of 2.2%, as it has in every recent year.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes have run below the ~23% book rate (635-751 paid a year) on bonus depreciation while capex exceeds D&A; 21% for two years, then the 23% book rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to a symmetric 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: the erosion it describes is already visible in the numbers (identical sales ex fuel +0.2% in Q2 fiscal 2026 against 2.9% the year before, H1 EBITDA down), though there is no solvency or refinancing risk, so it goes no higher. Base 50%: it is management's own framework at the bottom of its ranges. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three things at once, a share recovery under a CEO nine months into the job, sustained retail-media growth, and labour peace, from a starting point of 0.2% comps.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Base year FCF 3,299.0 is 2.3x the historical median 1,447.0
Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: regulatory single point of failure

sanity_check.fix_applied: One fix pass, 2026-11-15. No driver or value change: the trip is a denominator artifact (GAAP EPS 1.54 after the 2.5bn fulfilment-network impairment vs 4.85 adjusted; the actual trailing P/E was already 51.6x). Fix 1 (mid-cycle FCF) tested and recorded as inputs.mid_cycle_fcf = 2,373 (mid-point of median 1,447 and latest 3,299 owner FCF): base year-1 levered owner FCF is ~2.0bn, already below it, because the component build never compounds from last_fcf. Fix 2 (WACC premium): 7.5% already carries ~1.1 points over the computed ~6.4%, now itemised in wacc_rationale; not raised. Fix 3 (growth cap): base 1.8-2.5% vs 5-year revenue CAGR 2.2%. Fix 4 (exit cap): base terminal value 7.2x EBITDA vs 10-year average 7.9x. Passing the rule would need a base value <= ~50.8 (about 5.7x EV/adjusted EBITDA, below the 10-year minimum of 6.0x). Recorded as a known false positive; expected to clear when fiscal 2026 EPS replaces the impaired year. Detail in valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response.

implied_multiples_after_fix.note: Unchanged by design. Normalised at the base value of 69.84: P/E on adjusted EPS 4.85 = 14.4x; EV/adjusted EBITDA (8,080) = 7.1x; P/sales 0.28.
